title: soc_arch_map
description: INPUT CONTRACT for env.manifest.json's dut_facts.address_map and dut_facts.clock_reset sub-layers -- the 'address map / clock-reset topology from the existing SoC spec pipeline' fact source. Like register_map.schema.json, this file is NEVER generated by dv_harness/env_manifest.py: the generator only reads and validates it, and never invents an address decode range, a clock frequency or a reset polarity for a project it has not observed. A real project produces this file from its own SoC spec pipeline -- the architecture stage that already writes generated/01_architecture/{address decode, clock_reset_map, interface_map} -- or by converting an IP-XACT memoryMaps/ SoC integration spreadsheet to this shape. It is a documented input contract rather than a live extractor for the same reason register_map.schema.json is: dv_harness is the meta-harness and owns no SoC of its own, so there is nothing here to extract FROM, and a fabricated extractor would produce fabricated architecture. CORROBORATION, NOT AUTHORITY: env_manifest.py cross-checks every address_map entry's base against dut_facts.registers (see register_map_agreement in env_manifest.schema.json) and reports agreement/disagreement, but this file never silently overrides the register map and the register map never silently overrides this file -- a disagreement is surfaced, per CLAUDE.md's Source Authority Order, not resolved by whichever was loaded last.

kind.description: Where this file's content actually came from, e.g. 'soc_spec_pipeline_export', 'ip_xact_memory_map_conversion', 'integration_spec_transcription'.

address_map.description: One entry per decoded address region. Optional as a whole: a project that has a clock/reset topology but no address map yet simply omits this key, and dut_facts.address_map reports NOT_AVAILABLE with that honest reason rather than an empty-but-LOADED layer.

name.description: The decoded region's real name, matching the register-map block name where the two describe the same block -- that name match is what makes the register_map_agreement cross-check possible.

target.description: The RTL instance or block this region decodes to, e.g. 'chip.core.usb0'. Null when the spec genuinely does not say -- never a guessed instance path.

bus.description: Which fabric/bus this region is decoded on, e.g. 'APB', 'AXI4-Lite'.

evidence.description: Where this entry came from -- a decoder file:line, a spec section. Strongly recommended: an address region with no evidence citation cannot be re-checked by anyone.

clocks.description: One entry per clock domain. Optional as a whole (see address_map).

frequency_mhz.description: Null when the frequency is genuinely programmable or unspecified -- never a plausible-looking default.

domain.description: Clock-domain label used to group signals crossing into/out of it.

resets.description: One entry per reset. Optional as a whole (see address_map).

active_level.description: Required, and deliberately not defaulted: an assumed reset polarity is one of the cheapest ways to produce a testbench that holds a DUT in reset for an entire run while every gate still passes.

synchronous.description: True synchronous, false asynchronous, null when the spec genuinely does not say.

clock.description: Name of the clock in `clocks` this reset is synchronised to. Validated by env_manifest.py against `clocks`, so a reset naming a clock domain that does not exist is reported rather than silently carried.
